newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves and yearlings exported to the United States from Mexico sold 3-4 cents/lb higher than last week.
Exports for the week were estimated at 20,000 head into Texas and New Mexico states. Confirmed exports for the previous week totaled 14,193 head, against 6,771 head in the same week in 1996.
"Trade active, demand good. Bulk of supply consisted of medium and large steers weighing 300-600 lb," USDA said, adding 40 percent of sales were sold via video.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 86-96 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 76-86 cents/lb and 500-600 lb they were 74-78 cents/lb
Imports into Mexico were estimated to have totaled 2,500 head for the week with good demand for slaughter head, it added.
